idiom_name: protocol with extension defaults (+ class base for shared state)
implementation_notes: Swift classes inherit from exactly one superclass and the compiler checks overrides (override is mandatory, final seals a member or a class), so a layer with shared state can be modelled as a base class - but Swift has no abstract classes, so the base is an ordinary class unless its initializer is made unavailable, and nothing stops direct instantiation. For a stateless layer contract the idiomatic tool is a protocol with a default implementation in an extension, the documented substitute for multiple inheritance, which also lets structs and enums join the layer; protocols cannot declare stored properties, so shared state still belongs in a base class or a composed field. Combine both when needed: a protocol for the declared layer type and a class for the shared storage.
pitfalls: Protocol extensions cannot substitute for subclassing when state is shared: protocols have no stored properties, so a fully protocol-based layer duplicates state in every member.
A default implementation not overridden in a conforming base class cannot be overridden in its subclasses, so mixing class inheritance with protocol defaults can silently pin behavior.
Swift has no abstract classes: the base can be instantiated unless its init is made unavailable, and protocols are the only mechanism that forces implementations.
